title: Ferroni 2023 · Depersonalisation PPS preprint
citation: Ferroni, F., Arcuri, E., Ardizzi, M., Chinchella, N., Gallese, V., & Ciaunica, A. (2023). Lost in time and space? Multisensory processing of peripersonal space and time perception in Depersonalisation. PsyArXiv, version 1.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.cohort: 70 adults stratified into groups of 35 using low (≤20) and high (≥50) Cambridge Depersonalisation Scale scores.
published_method.sessions: Counterbalance the PPS and mental time travel tasks on the same day. The time travel task measures temporal judgment in the same study and has a distinct design.
published_method.response: Detect a single pulse applied to the hairy side of the right index finger, while blindfolded with right palm down. Ignore the looming and flat sounds and respond quickly to touch.
published_method.analysis: Compare reaction times across five sound-relative delays. Estimate PSE and DL from trimmed reaction-time means and compare the score groups.
published_method.confirmed: Main text describes looming and flat cues, with Digitimer DS3 electrodes on the hairy dorsal right index finger.

provisional_supplement.scope: Appendix settings occur alongside unrelated clinical sample and pre/post training language. The main preprint describes a different population and design. The printed counts also conflict.

task_sequence_rules.value: Respond to touch quickly, ignore sound. Appendix describes left-index laptop button and repeats after misses.

tactile_stimulus.gap: Main article names constant-current stimulator and calls the pulse constant-voltage. Pulse duration occurs in the inconsistent appendix. The appendix's current ranges are labeled controls versus schizophrenia and cannot be assigned to the DP groups.

soa_table.gap: Main results confirm five ordered D labels. Numerical offsets come from the inconsistent appendix.

baseline_strategy.gap: The reported silence-relative timing comes from the appendix.
